# Parley v0.1.45

Two changes: Flexible no longer restricts shell commands for any vendor, and
the v0.1.44 Approvals choice now actually reaches a host Codex pane.

## Flexible carries no shell restriction

Flexible allowed project tools but still asked before local processes, and
Claude can only express that as an ask rule for all of Bash. So a Claude pane
on Flexible, the default for new panes, prompted before every shell command,
`parley` included, and no allow rule could carve `parley` out: Claude
evaluates deny, then ask, then allow, whatever the rule's specificity, and a
scripted session proved it. Flexible now allows both execution rules. No
vendor receives a shell restriction from it: Claude gets only the allow rules
for Parley's command, so `parley` runs without a prompt and every other
command keeps Claude's own acceptEdits prompt. Default and Workspace folders
still ask, and Review only still denies. An existing Flexible pane picks this
up on its next start or restart.

## Host Codex now receives the auto-review choice

A host Codex pane's arguments come from Parley's Codex-native permission
rules, not from the generic launch plan that the review displays and that
container and non-Codex launches use. v0.1.44 put the new
`approvals_reviewer = auto_review` setting in the plan only, so the review said
a host Codex pane would use auto review while its launch carried nothing. The
setting now travels with the Codex-native rules, so a host Codex pane started
with **Vendor's automatic reviewer** gets it. A pane whose own Codex config
already sets auto review saw no difference, which is why the acceptance runs
did not catch it.

The check that walks every vendor's launch now also builds the host Codex
arguments and was watched failing without the fix. Its pair matcher had been
stopping at the first `-c`, which on a Codex launch is the permissions table;
it now looks at every adjacent pair.

## Corrected wording

The v0.1.43 notes and scenario P3.3 said a Claude host member on Flexible runs
`parley` without a prompt. That was wrong. Flexible asks before local
processes, Claude carries that as an ask rule for all of Bash, and Claude's
ask rules beat allow rules even in auto mode; a scripted Claude session proved
it. Only Broad workspace, or a custom profile allowing both execution rules,
gets the `parley` allow rules. P3.3 and the checklist now say so.

## Compatibility

Nothing else changed. Agent protocol unchanged at 32. An existing Codex pane
picks up the setting on its next start or restart.

Validated: 346 native checks, 53 Node tests, public scan, platform scan and
build.

Unnotarized test beta: ad-hoc signed without the hardened runtime, not
notarized, no automatic updates. Install only from the expected GitLab
release after checking SHA256SUMS.
